body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim) announced that it will operate the Seoul Integrated Pavilion at CES 2026, which takes place in Las Vegas, the United States, from Tuesday, January 6, to Friday, January 9. Following last year, SBA will also host and expand a CES-first, cross-national cooperation–based networking event, the Global Innovation Forum (GIF), on January 7, positioning it as a platform to lead the convergence of the global startup ecosystem.

The forum is designed to provide Seoul-based startups with outstanding technological capabilities and growth potential an opportunity to directly engage with key players in the global startup ecosystem, helping transform CES participation into tangible global business opportunities and enabling startups to shine on the world stage. In particular, the forum is expected to draw strong interest from startups and ecosystem stakeholders seeking global expansion, as it offers a rare opportunity to experience investment, promotion, and networking in one place.

The Global Innovation Forum was conceived as a networking platform that uses CES, the world’s largest exhibition, as a bridge to enable startup ecosystems from different countries to communicate organically beyond national borders. Its origin dates back to 2025, when it launched under the name “Seoul Innovation Forum,” with collaboration among five national pavilions: Japan, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Taiwan, and South Korea (Seoul). As the first event built on solidarity among Eureka Park–participating countries at CES, the Seoul Innovation Forum carried particular significance. It brought together leading startup ecosystem players from each country to explore practical cooperation measures and was widely regarded as a successful first step toward strengthening competitiveness as global startups.

Building on this success, the event has been renamed the Global Innovation Forum starting in 2026 to provide participating startups with more stable and expanded opportunities for global collaboration. The forum’s highlight, the IR pitching competition, has been significantly strengthened through an enhanced judging panel. In addition to the technology promotion effect achieved through global media exposure, the competition now incorporates rigorous business evaluation by international venture capital firms. Through this structure, participating companies are expected to gain opportunities for accelerated growth by simultaneously gaining brand visibility, attracting investment, and receiving market validation.

The 2026 Global Innovation Forum will be held on January 7, the second day of the exhibition, at the Emperors Ballroom of Caesars Palace in Las Vegas. The event is organized through cooperation among the host organizations Seoul Business Agency (SBA), Taiwan Tech Arena (TTA), Switzerland Global Enterprise (S-GE), Israel Economic and Trade Office, Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), Quebec Government Office of Canada, and Business France.

body.x: The forum will open with an IR pitching competition featuring startups selected by each participating country. This competition serves as a core program that draws strong attention from investors, media, and industry stakeholders, as promising startups carefully chosen by national startup support organizations present their technologies and business models directly on the global stage.

Each participating country—South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Israel, Japan, Canada, and France—will select outstanding startups to showcase before global investors and media, providing them with opportunities to expand international partnerships. Through this IR pitching competition, which combines media influence with the expertise of venture capital firms, participating companies are expected to achieve tangible outcomes beyond simple promotion, including market validation and investment connections.

As the forum’s centerpiece, the IR pitching competition will serve as a declarative stage where top startups from seven countries, media influence through venture capital firms’ expertise, and participating companies are expected to achieve tangible outcomes. South Korea, Japan, and France will prove their value on a global platform. This stage, where national innovation capabilities converge, will function as a bridgehead for expanding international partnerships. Through an advanced evaluation process involving both media and venture capital firms, participating companies are expected to achieve enhanced brand recognition and meaningful access to capital simultaneously.

Award-winning companies that demonstrate innovation and vision during the competition will receive prize money and trophies in their respective award categories. The awards are divided into the Grand Award for first place, the Scale-up Award for second place, and the Impact Award for third place, with prize money of USD 3,000, USD 2,000, and USD 1,000, respectively.

In addition, the Global Innovation Forum will host panel discussions featuring representatives from each country, creating a knowledge-sharing platform to discuss the latest trends and share know-how across the global startup ecosystem. This is expected to strengthen policy-level solidarity among countries beyond individual company scale-up efforts. A networking session that allows participants to interact freely will also be a key element in turning forum participation into concrete business results. The teamwork created by bringing together media, venture capital firms, startups, and startup support organizations in one place is expected to open new opportunities for startups to enter markets.

Hyunwoo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency, presented his vision for the forum, saying, “We will grow this into a representative cooperation model that connects the global startup ecosystem into one by using CES as a springboard.”
